messages:
alexa-docs: hey team — opening a small PR to fold a few on-prem docs fixes into the installer guide and the private deployment quickstart. items: nftables+iptables SNAT examples, a micro-guide for offline cert bundles, a brief HSM permission troubleshooting note, and a windows conn-checker snippet. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4629 :wave:

kevin-ops: thanks alexa. quick asks: 1) make it clear which ports need cluster-internal vs provider-internal access (source ranges), 2) show an example of preserving existing NAT rules when applying our SNAT, and 3) add a comment about Jumbo frames/MTU when using overlay networks.

maria-engineering: i'll add the windows node example. using powershell + environment proxy is the most common ask from support right now. will paste and link to the conn-checker page.

maria-engineering: ```
# PowerShell example for conn-checker and quickstart
$env:HTTPS_PROXY = 'http://proxy.corp.local:8080'
$env:RW_KEY = 'REDACTED'
node -e "const {Client} = require('@redwood/inference'); const c = new Client({apiKey:process.env.RW_KEY}); c.text.create({model:'redwood-small',input:'test'}).then(r=>console.log(r)).catch(e=>console.error(e))"
```

jon-ml: for the HSM note: call out the common permissions trap — if the HSM device node (e.g., /dev/hsm0) is owned by root:root but our runtime runs as redwood-user, rotation may fail with CKR_USER_NOT_LOGGED_IN or device open errors. recommend a systemd tmpfiles.d entry and show a chown example.

jon-ml: example: ```
# ensure runtime can access HSM
chown root:redwood-runtime /dev/hsm0
chmod 660 /dev/hsm0
# systemd tmpfiles.d snippet (create /etc/tmpfiles.d/hsm.conf)
# w /dev/hsm0 - - - 0660 root redwood-runtime
```

kevin-ops: nice. can we also include a short iptables-save/restore snippet so customers who manage iptables via config can commit atomically?

alexa-docs: added both nft and iptables atomic examples in the network appendix. kept the iptables approach as save/restore tarball so it doesn't clobber provider rules. also added a short callout about cloud NAT (provider NAT may reroute SNAT behavior).

docs-lint-bot: link-check FAILED: internal anchor "conn-checker#windows" not found.

maria-engineering: fixing anchors now. also found a stray backtick in the quickstart that broke a fenced block — pushing a tiny fix to the same branch.

docs-lint-bot: re-run: link-check OK. markdown-style: OK. accessibility: warning 1 (table lacks header).

kevin-ops: small content suggestion: under SNAT example add a snippet showing how to prepend rules to preserve the customer's existing iptables-chain ordering (so we don't accidentally drop traffic).

alexa-docs: done. i added a short note and an example using iptables -I to insert at the top. also added the MTU note (jumbo frames may be required for certain on-prem NICs). corrected casing on MTU per linter.

jon-ml: i pushed a short migration pointer for customers going from file-based PKCS#11 modules to an HSM daemon architecture (we'll link to the longer migration guide later). includes a checklist: copy key ACLs, update module path, update service account.

maria-engineering: +1 on the checklist. i also extended the windows snippet to include a timeout override and an example displaying the full TLS error chain to help with internal CA setups.

alexa-docs: thanks all — merging once CI passes. final pre-merge TODO: add a one-liner about rotating HSM certs while preserving active sessions (link to vendor doc).

alexa-docs: merged (commit d5b2f8a). if followups needed, open a tiny PR referencing this thread so we can keep the main installer doc stable. :tada:
